subject: research/buildbot-carryphase
professional: a humanoid locomotion and whole-body control researcher (ZMP/MPC walking, inverse dynamics on Unitree-class robots) refereeing for ICRA/Humanoids or RA-L; they would check first that the dynamics are right (wrench decomposition, load force, centre of pressure), then whether a prescribed uncompensated LIPM gait says anything about what the robot can do, and what is new relative to payload-walking and loco-manipulation work

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 -m pytest -q tests` (9 passed, 28 s, Menagerie clone fetched). Recomputed without the project's scoring code: (1) static waist-pitch torque of the G1 at the slow-step mid pose (L 0.05, T 4) from the model's subtree mass and COM about the joint axis, cross product with gravity plus the load at the mean palm position: 28.15 N m (ratio 0.563) unloaded and 47.39 N m (0.948) at 4 kg, against the model's torque ratios 0.5662 and 0.9531 (0.5 to 0.6 percent apart, and the limit is 50 N m); (2) integrated the LIPM equation x''=g/z x forward in time (explicit Euler, dt 1e-6) from the closed-form initial velocity in lipm_x: x(T) = 0.09999790 vs the expected L/2 = 0.1; (3) rate arithmetic by hand: G1 3 kg at 10 m, pp 6 s: trip 6+10/0.2+10/0.25 = 96 s = 37.5/h (reported 38); person range 138 to 532/h = 6+20 s trip at 1.0 m/s with one piece and 6+14.29 s at 1.4 m/s with three; break-even 40 m, pp 6, three pieces at 1.2 m/s: target trip 24.2 s per piece, walk 18.2 s, 2*40/18.2 = 4.39 m/s (reported 4.39; 12.86 and 5.62 checked the same way); (4) from results.json (636 rows) recounted the headline tallies: G1 flat 216 cases, 140 with torque ratio > 1, 140 with negative COP margin, 51 feasible, 1 IK failure; H1 181, 202, 12, 124; the stored `ok` flag equals the conjunction of its stored fields for all 636 rows; (5) re-ran one grid cell through score(): G1 0 kg, L 0.2, T 0.8 gives ratio 0.62242 and COP margin 2.12 mm against stored 0.62242 and 2.12 mm. Not independently checked: the dynamic part (inertial torques at speed, swing leg), the COP sign convention at speed, and any real-robot number; the static check covers only the gravity term.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: 636-case sweep (results.json has 636 rows), sections A to G of results.txt (all present and consistent with the JSON), ramps at 4.76 and 7.13 deg, step-up 5 to 20 cm, H1 and G1, rate and break-even tables, experiments/figure.png exists (content not inspected), 9 tests (five need the clone, as stated), project.json card present. The sibling buildbot-carry exists. Not verified: the live page URL. Not listed in PROGRAMMES.md or PROJECTS.md by name. The README is explicit about what is not done (falls, drops, energy per item, policy), so those are not counted against it. Minor: 'limits,, as in' double comma.
evidence.verification: Test command above: 9 passed. Mutation A (ok threshold `R.max() <= 1.0` raised to 1.3 in score()): 9 passed, NOT caught. Mutation B (load force divided by 3 instead of 2 in the hand wrench, model.py:264): caught, test_load_adds_its_weight_to_the_foot_force failed. Mutation C (sign of the COP x coordinate flipped, model.py:277): 9 passed, NOT caught, although the COP margin decides feasibility for 140 of 216 G1 cases and is the headline explanation. All reverted with git checkout; git status clean. Tests check LIPM endpoints and equation of motion, foot force equals weight (rel 6 percent), load adds weight (rel 15 percent), slope cos and tan, fast-big fails vs slow-small passes, heavier load raises ratio, and trip arithmetic. No test pins a COP margin, a torque ratio, or a feasibility threshold; the only guard on the sweep's outputs is that results.txt was generated once.
evidence.craft: Read src/buildbot_carryphase/model.py (292 lines), rate.py, tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py. Good: gravity is changed under try/finally and restored; docstrings state what is not modelled; frozen constants named; the experiment is deterministic. Defects: reaches into buildbot_payload's private helpers (P._bid, _point, _jac, _lm) from a sibling project, so a rename there breaks this silently; `sw` in Setup.__post_init__ and `J` in ik() are unused; IK failure is returned as a residual and collapsed into 'not feasible' (124 of H1's 216 cases), so reachability and dynamics failures share one bucket; best_speed in rate.py selects payload by float equality; rate.table hard-codes the three cases; sys.path manipulation in tests and run.py; a polynomial fit of degree 8 to 13 IK samples with no check beyond a reported fit error (not gated by ok); per-case work is recomputed from scratch with a new MjData per call (about 12 min for the sweep).
evidence.claims: Checked against files: headline G1 speeds 0.25/0.20/0.10/none and H1 0.15/0.10/0.07/none equal results.txt section B and the JSON; the standing limits 4.6 and 18.8 kg are section A; '140 of 216' is verified from the JSON; ramp and step-up claims equal sections C and D (G1 4/4 at 10 cm, 1/4 at 15 cm); '4.4 to 13 m/s over 40 m' equals 4.39 to 12.86 recomputed by hand; '5 to 38 pieces/hour against 35 to 532' equals section F. Honest limits: lower bounds, not a policy, not a safety case, vendor 2 m/s marked unverified, step width and handling time marked as assumptions and swept. Weaker: (a) the break-even for a one-piece person is 1.2 m/s by construction, a tautology presented as a finding; (b) section F pits a G1 holding 3 kg (a light piece) against a person moving 5.8 kg pieces, mixed masses; (c) Bohannon and Andrews speeds were read from a summary and handout, said so; (d) the claim that 1:8 is the steepest slope allowed for existing sites under ADA 405.2 was not checked here; (e) the page title asks whether a stock robot can carry a stud as fast as a labourer, but the measured speeds come from a gait with no trunk compensation and say little about the answer, as the README itself concedes.
evidence.fitness: Could a researcher build on it? Partly. The pipeline (IK at 13 instants, polynomial smoothing, mj_inverse, stance wrench from the six base rows, torque and COP scoring) is a compact, reusable way to screen a prescribed motion against Menagerie limits, and the static decomposition is right to within 0.6 percent. But the central output, a maximum speed of 0.1 to 0.25 m/s, is a property of the chosen gait (COP fixed at foot centre, zero double support, no angular momentum, no trunk or arm compensation), not of the robot: the vendor demonstrates about 2 m/s and the repository's own README says the centre of pressure leaves the sole before torque binds. Nearest prior work, cited here from memory and not verified: Kajita et al. 2001 and the ZMP preview-control line (Kajita 2003) which solve exactly the COP-on-sole problem this gait ignores; Unitree G1 and H1 loco-manipulation and carrying work in RL (e.g. HumanPlus, OmniH2O-style whole-body policies) and MuJoCo Playground G1 locomotion; payload-aware whole-body MPC for humanoids. None is cited except Kajita 2001. The result is therefore not new beyond the engineering fact that a naive pendulum gait is slow, and the part that matters to the stated user (can a robot match a labourer) is decided by trip arithmetic with unsourced inputs. The H1 half is confounded by IK reach failures (124 of 216).
evidence.domain: Compared against standard humanoid practice: ZMP preview control or centroidal MPC would place the COP on the sole by moving the trunk and arms (the README's own 'Next steps'), include double support and swing-leg impact, and test with a whole-body controller in simulation (MuJoCo Playground, Isaac). A locomotion researcher would sign off on the inverse-dynamics bookkeeping (the load as m(g - a_hand) split between hands, stance wrench from the base rows, tilted gravity for slopes all check out) but not on interpreting L/T as a speed limit; they would also ask for actuator torque-speed curves rather than a flat peak torque, a grip and swinging-load model for a 2.4 m stud, and a friction limit rather than a report. On the labour side a construction ergonomist would want a time study, not 3 pieces at 5.8 kg under the NIOSH constant as an assumption. The ankle-roll-free H1 treatment is described but makes H1 numbers uninformative.

defects.what: The headline speeds (0.25 m/s G1, 0.15 m/s H1) are a property of an uncompensated pendulum gait that the project itself says fails on COP before torque; they are lower bounds of unknown looseness and the page's question (can the robot match a labourer) is not answered by them.

Seeded mutations not caught: flipping the sign of the COP x coordinate and loosening the feasibility torque threshold from 1.0 to 1.3 both left 9 tests passing. No test pins a COP margin, a torque ratio or the ok rule that decides 140 of 216 G1 cases.

Carry-rate table compares a G1 holding 3 kg against a person moving 5.8 kg pieces, and the one-piece break-even (1.2 m/s) is true by construction; the H1 half is dominated by IK reach failures (124 of 216) that are reported in the same bucket as dynamic infeasibility.
Depends on private helpers of a sibling project (_bid, _point, _jac, _lm) and uses sys.path injection; a rename in buildbot_payload breaks it silently.
Unused variables (`sw` in Setup, `J` in ik) and a double comma in the README ('limits,, as in').
Smoothing fit error is reported but does not gate feasibility; flat peak torque limits with no torque-speed curve; step width 0.15 m and clearance 0.05 m are unsourced and not swept.
Closest prior work (ZMP preview control, G1 loco-manipulation policies) is not cited and no novelty claim is made; not listed in PROGRAMMES.md.

verdict: A careful, honest, reproducible simulation note whose mechanics are right: the 9 tests pass, the static waist torque recomputed from the model's masses matches the project's inverse-dynamics ratio to 0.6 percent (0.948 vs 0.953 at 4 kg), the LIPM orbit integrates to its endpoint, the rate and break-even numbers recompute by hand, and the 636-row JSON reproduces every tally in the README and a re-run cell to five digits. So it is correct and finished. It does not meet the bar. Verification is 2: of three seeded mutations in core scoring logic only the load-force one was caught; a flipped COP sign and a loosened torque threshold passed, though they decide the headline. The deeper limit is fitness and domain: the speeds describe a deliberately uncompensated gait, not the robot, so a locomotion researcher would use the inverse-dynamics pipeline but not the speed numbers, and the 'loses to a labourer' conclusion rests on unsourced trip arithmetic that the project concedes holds whatever the gait does. Cheapest improvements: add tests pinning the COP margin and the ok rule on a hand-computed case, split IK failures from dynamic failures, and add a ZMP-preview trunk compensation to turn the lower bound into a ceiling.
